title: SAGENet: Sub-cluster Aggregation Guided Enhancement for Imbalanced Attributed Graph Clustering
abstract: Attributed graph clustering methods often suffer from substantial performance degradation when applied to real-world data, primarily due to the pervasive challenge of class imbalance. In such scenarios, majority classes tend to dominate the learned representation space, suppressing minority classes and undermining their discriminability. This distortion is paradoxically aggravated by message passing—a foundational component of Graph Convolutional Networks (GCNs)—as it propagates and magnifies existing bias through topological connections, thereby obfuscating the decision boundaries of minority clusters. To address this, we propose the Sub-cluster Aggregation Guided Enhancement Network (SAGENet), a framework that leverages sub-cluster aggregation to guide representation enhancement. Our approach over-clusters data into fine-grained sub-clusters, applies dual-frequency filtering to preserve structural information, and merges them into target clusters via a learnable assignment. The resulting aggregation process provides guidance signals for representation learning, enabling reliable sample selection with class-balanced weights and an adaptive push-away loss that explicitly separates majority and minority representations. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that our method consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines.
